sections.overview: This widely distributed seed bug is found across warm parts of Europe, Africa and Asia.
sections.identification: Adults have a conspicuous red-and-black pattern. They also have paired thoracic glands that produce defensive secretions.
sections.habitat: It is often found on its food plants, including milkweeds such as Calotropis and other seed-bearing plants.
sections.diet: It is phytophagous and uses a range of host plants. Field reports describe adults and nymphs feeding on seeds. Laboratory choice tests found a preference for Calotropis procera.
sections.behavior: The bug can incorporate plant cardiac glycosides into defensive secretions that deter predators.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs, which hatch into nymphs that pass through successive stages before adulthood.
sections.ecology: Field reports show that this bug also feeds on crop plants, including cucurbits. In France, it is recorded in warm, dry habitats such as fallows, roadsides and dunes.
sections.conservation: The French FAUNA catalogue reports that the species has not been assessed in a Red List.
